chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the one who divorces [his wife] during a state of purity in a single session after session, three times. He said: It counts as one.
ai.seo_question: Does triple divorce in one session count as three divorces or one?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the Shia jurisprudential position that triple divorce pronounced in a single session constitutes only one revocable divorce (ṭalāq al-sunna), contrasting with the Sunni view of it being three distinct divorces. By specifying the condition of 'ṭuhr' (purity), the Imam emphasizes the procedural correctness of the pronouncement, ensuring it aligns with the Prophetic tradition rather than being a hasty, irrevocable act. This ruling has significant practical implications for marital reconciliation, as the couple may resume relations during the waiting period (ʿiddah) without a new contract.
